layout.title: 98″ wall TV · 4-seat sofa · 6-seat dining table off the island
notes: Dining by the kitchen: a 72″ × 36″ table runs south from the island with three chairs a side, every chair 36″+ of pull-out room.
Living by the lake: a 108″ four-seat sofa floats facing the TV wall, a 98″ TV on it, coffee table between.

verdicts.summary: Strong, balanced; loses a little on east chairs crowding the Bath 2 route and the 12½–13½ ft viewing distance.
feedback: TV fills 27–31°; a 96″ sofa at x 40–78 would reach ~34° but crushes the west chairs’ pull-out (~24″).
East chairs at x 138–162 leave 35″ at Bath 2; a pulled-out chair blocks the office route. Use 2 east chairs at y 150–194 plus a south-end chair.
Dead strips: behind the sofa (x 0–25) and the south-east floor.
The 16″-high floating console hides the outlet at 16″; raise it ~4″.

verdicts.summary: The right balance for this room; the column and island keep the far seat at 27°.
feedback: Every nudge it measured is worse: 7″ east costs chair pull-out, a 5-seat sofa pinches the balcony or drops a seat below prime.
The south-west chair sits 2″ from seat 1’s feet when both are occupied.
Rug 1″ from the column: move its center to (108, 84).
Console covers the outlet’s lower half: mount it at 18–28″ and raise the TV center to 56″.
Brief errors: column clearance is 4″, not 3″; the 49″ island figure is corner to corner.

verdicts.summary: Right macro zoning, but seat 1 overlaps the south-west dining chair (15″ gap, 2″ past legroom), the rug stops short, and the TV is raised to 52″ just to clear a chair back.
feedback: Alternative A (66″ table, 104″ sofa, 10×8 rug, console top at 20″): est. 9.2.
Alternative B: sofa east of the column (x 82–120), 85–92″ TV at 8 ft (38–46°), dining pull-out 48″, reading nook in the lake bay: est. 9.5.
Chair pull-out ignores the sofa sitter’s legroom; sightline check assumes 34″ chair backs.
Console bisects the outlet; brief says 3″ to the column, actually 4″.

verdicts.summary: Nails 6-seat dining and plan compliance, but the island dining forces a long viewing throw (27–31° fill).
feedback: The 98″ is at 27–31°; seat 1 at 27°.
Corner-TV L (G1) reaches 31–40° and 5 prime seats but has no dining.
4 couch seats meets the minimum, not the ideal 5.

verdicts.summary: Meets the seating, TV and dining targets; no buildable improvement found without a material trade-off.
feedback: A seated west diner leaves ~15″ to the sofa; routes are not passage behind occupied chairs.
Sightline check uses empty chair backs, not seated diners.
Tape the column and balcony jamb before ordering.

changes: Sofa moves east of the column (x 82–120, y 8–116), 8 ft from the TV wall, so it no longer overlaps the dining chairs in y.
TV becomes the 85″ Samsung M70HB already in the TV list: 38–42° of view, more than the 98″ gave at 13 ft.
All six dining chairs get 48″ of pull-out room even with the sofa full.
Console raised to 10–20″ so it frames the outlet instead of cutting it; rug clear of the column; reading nook in the freed lake bay.

layout.title: 85″ wall TV at 8 ft · 4-seat sofa east of the column · 6-seat dining off the island
notes: The sofa moves east of the column, 8 ft from the TV wall, so an 85″ screen fills 38–42° of view: more picture than a 98″ at 13 ft (28–31°).
Dining stays by the kitchen: the 72″ × 36″ table off the island with three chairs a side, now 48″ of pull-out room each.
The freed lake corner behind the sofa becomes a reading nook: a swivel lounge chair and lamp by the column, the balcony route behind.

components.label: Floating console (10–20″ up, frames the outlet)

verdicts.summary: Four prime seats, a 6-seat table and a clean plan; two small, cheap fixes remain.
feedback: 85″ is 13″ under the cap; a 98″ here fills ~48.6° from the middle seats, which is a taste call.
Turn the swivel chair east and it becomes a fifth (good, ~25°) TV seat.
The console at 10–20″ hides the 16″ outlet rather than framing it: use a shelf at 20–24″ or a back cutout.
“Island clearance 79″” cannot be walked: the table sits 1.4″ from the island by design.

verdicts.summary: Four prime 25″ seats at 8 ft, an 85″ picture at 38–42°, and a six-seat table whose chairs pull out more than 5 ft.
feedback: Only change: turn the reading chair 180° (rot 225) toward the lake.
Any TV up to 92″ keeps all four seats prime; 98″ drops the middle two to good.
Real pull-out is 61″ east and 102″ west; the tool caps at 48″.
Rug label says 8×10; it is 8′ × 9′4″.

verdicts.summary: Resolves every round-1 crowding, sightline and console issue, gives every chair 48″+ and turns the lake bay into a reading nook.
feedback: A 56″ × 24″ coffee table at (149, 62) opens the sofa gap to 17″: est. 9.8.
A standard 8′ × 9′ rug at (137, 62) lines up with the sofa ends.
The console needs an open back bay to truly frame the outlet.

verdicts.summary: Trades 13″ of diagonal for all-prime viewing at ~8 ft, fixes the sofa/dining clash and fully delivers six-seat dining.
feedback: A 92″ panel at the same mount keeps all four seats prime (41–46°): est. 9.5.
The brief overstated 85″ as the prime ceiling here.

verdicts.summary: Excellent use of the room; meets the seating, TV and dining goals.
feedback: The rotated nook chair leaves ~27″ to the sofa back: move it to (25, 80) and the lamp to (14, 115) for ~34″.
A fully pulled-out east chair and the 37″ route share floor.

changes: Goal met: 4 of 5 councillors at 9 or above, so H2 stands as submitted.

Suggested refinements not applied, because each would be a new submission: turn the nook chair toward the lake or move it to (25, 80); a 56″ × 24″ coffee table; a standard 8′ × 9′ rug; an open-back console bay at the outlet; a 92″ TV if one is sold.
